objective: Eliminate the three-component two-terminal interface pattern by a planar single-arc completion, and audit the remaining two-side patterns.

atomic_claims.text: For nonadjacent separator terminals, any proper union of components plus either one terminal arc remains a smaller simple planar orientation.
A vertex-minimum counterexample has exactly two components behind any two-vertex separator.
For nonadjacent terminals the two availability sets are {D} and {P,M}; for a terminal arc s-to-t they are {D} and {P}.
A forced-different side with nonadjacent terminals contains a directed two-edge path between the terminals in at least one direction.

assumptions: Global vertex-count minimality in the entire frozen planar-orientation class.
C03 no-cut-vertex argument and C05 exact two-terminal interface are used as proof-draft dependencies.
Finite simple graph orientations; only one new terminal direction is inserted at a time.
Basic planar minor closure and finite directed-cycle facts.
risks: This refinement does not assert 3-connectivity or prove the root conjecture.
Colorings for the two opposite single-arc augmentations may differ.
Vertex identification can create a digon; its absence is separately assumed and proved where used.
Natural-language draft only; no mathematical execution or verifier receipt.
